items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'what if' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how cool this story is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement ('WOW' energy), build excitement through each line, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. 'again?' in the first line gets a playful, knowing, excited lift. 'But that's not even the weirdest part' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. 'and failed every time' is a comic deadpan drop. Costa Rica's reply 'No army... no thanks!' is a cheeky, chill little voice-wink. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Pronounce Honduras as hon-DOOR-us, El Salvador as el SAL-vuh-dor, Guatemala as gwah-tuh-MAH-luh, Costa Rica as KOH-stuh REE-kuh.
lines: Narrator
What if these five countries became one... again?
Narrator
Yes, again. They've already been one country.
Narrator
In eighteen twenty-three, all five formed one republic.
Narrator
But they fought so much... it fell apart in under twenty years.
Narrator
So what would this country get today?
Narrator
About forty-eight million people... more than Canada.
Narrator
More land than Germany... touching two oceans.
Narrator
And look at their flags. Blue, white, blue. All from the old one.
Narrator
They even share a birthday: September fifteenth.
Narrator
But that's not even the weirdest part.
Narrator
Honduras kept five stars on its flag... hoping all five reunite.
Narrator
And El Salvador's constitution still says: rebuild the republic!
Narrator
They've tried three more times... and failed every time.
Narrator
Then there's the capital. Guatemala City... or San Salvador?
Narrator
Costa Rica's reply? No army... no thanks!
Narrator
So... one country, or five? Because honestly...
